newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerians jailed in Paris for identity card fraud.
newsitem.headline: Algerians jailed in Paris for identity card fraud.

text.p: A Paris court sentenced six Algerian men to between five months and five years in jail on Friday for trafficking in false identity papers for Algeria's banned Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).

The Algerians were detained in northern France and the Paris region between 1994 and 1996 as part of a network sending counterfeit identity papers to rebels fighting the military-backed government in the North African country.

In raids on their homes, investigators found 551 false Algerian identity cards, 606 false certificates showing the bearer had done Algerian military service, an assault rifle, several hundred cartridges and some weapons parts.
Larbi Beddiaf, 57, and El Hadj Chaib-Eddour, 41, were sentenced to five years each on charges of criminal conspiracy linked to a terrorist group and trafficking in counterfeit documents.
At the trial last month, prosecutors said they were respectively the organiser and the recipient of the false papers.
Hassan Tobal, 28, and Ahmed Seba, 30, were sentenced to four years in jail as accomplices. Two other accomplices, Mohamed Sedjerari, 48, and Hakim Beddiaf, 21, got sentences of five months in jail.
Prosecutors had urged prison terms of three to six years for the seven, who faced a maximum 10 years in jail.
Algeria's Islamic rebels took up arms after the military-backed government cancelled 1992 elections that FIS candidates were poised to win. An estimated 60,000 people have since died in the struggle.
